svg.aria-label: How an order moves through ModelEx - collectibles example
svg.title: How an order moves through ModelEx - collectibles example
svg.text: How an order moves through ModelEx
Worked example from the collectibles market (scenarios/collectible_orderbook.json)
INV_A wants to BUY 600 units of FRAC-CAR-1962-GT, paying up to £42.55 each (GTC)
Sent over the JSON API (or FIX) and translated into one standard internal order
② Validation: 16 checks, always in the same order
The first check that fails rejects the order, so the same mistake always gives the same reason.
Is it well-formed, new, and a real item?
Can this item trade right now, with this kind of order?
Is there a price, and is the quantity allowed?
Example order passes every check → accepted. INV_A receives a NEW report.
Buy 2 of the one-off art print
Sender gets a REJECTED report + reason
③ Session check: what phase is this item in right now?
Collectibles day: 09:00 pre-open · 10:00 continuous · 20:00 pre-close · 20:30 closed
Nothing trades yet: the order waits.
When the phase ends, all crossing
orders trade at ONE price. → diagram 3
Trades straight away with the best
price on the other side; equal prices
Anything not traded rests here, sorted
GTC orders stay for the next day.
⑥ Responses go back to both sides
Sellers: TRADE reports of their own. A public Trade record is published.
Each message is translated back to JSON or FIX for the participant.
per item: open, high, low, last,
Watches ② ③ ④ ⑤ ⑥
